title: Locked Drawer
warm:
Locked drawer opened under Nolan Greer's watching eyes in the Crownspire penthouse, wood and metal yielding with a soft click that sounded louder than Detective Imani Brooks's badge flash downstairs. [player_name]—early thirties, she/her, neighbor across the hall—felt the soft alibi rearrange itself around her fingertips. Full cooperation had a smell: rain-money cologne, Vivienne's unused perfume ghosting from the master bath, oak from the wine ring still nested on marble.

"Open it," Nolan said. Mid-forties, finance and tech holding, brutal charm never clean-cut. His cufflinks clicked once—the tell that lived when Vivienne's name entered a room—and then stayed still, as if even metal understood this was not a night for easy lies. "Brooks is climbing toward homicide interest without a body. Soft still keeps you from becoming the sharpest edge she finds. Soft also means you stop pretending you haven't wanted to see what I lock away."

Inside: not a corpse, not a confession labeled for Layer 10. A silent-partner file with dates that rhymed too cleanly with absences money preferred—travel language, NDA stubs Marcus Pell would recognize by typeface, calendar gaps that made Vivienne's weekly-to-monthly-to-gone cadence feel like an older method wearing a wife's name. [player_name] did not invent death. She did not invent willing leave, paid vanish, or staging. Four fates stayed open on purpose. The file only proved Nolan knew how absence could be purchased, managed, and explained.

Wind sheer pressed floor-to-ceiling glass. Elevator chime trembled in the private shaft. Somewhere below, Rhea Quinn was choosing how much slate to surrender; somewhere in a black car, Pell was polishing traveling until it reflected nothing. [player_name] lifted the top sheet and felt her throat close around complicity that tasted like protection.

"You wanted me soft," she said. "Soft is not blind."

"Soft is selective," Nolan answered, almost kind. "Choose what you carry out of that drawer. The silent-partner rhyme—or the gap in your own story you still refuse to inventory for me. Both keep Brooks warmer. Neither settles Vivienne."

She catalogued the drawer the way Brooks would: paper, dates, methods, no settled body. Soft alibi had fingerprints now. Across the hall, her own apartment waited with clearer conscience and colder sheets. Here, full coop meant becoming co-author of silence that might rhyme with a missing wife without confirming which door Vivienne had taken.

Nolan stood close enough that cologne found her pulse. "If you take the silent-partner file into the next hour, you walk with my oldest teeth showing. If you choose the gap in your story instead, you keep one night unnamed even after unlocking wood with me watching. Consequence either way."

[player_name] set the sheet down carefully, as if marble could bruise. Hope and dread shared the wine ring. Vivienne nowhere and everywhere—willing, paid, dead, or staging. Brooks's colder paper rising without a corpse. Soft cooperation had stopped being temporary the moment the lock turned under his stare.

She thought of the night she had almost named and did not—the black car too long at the curb, a bag by a door, perfume capped mid-exit. Full coop could still leave footnotes. Or it could spend the silent-partner rhyme as the next verb of pressure. Choice labels waited as consequence: risk the old absence method, or risk the private gap she had worn like underwear under cover.

Crownspire held its hush. Cufflink stillness. Perfume. Badge rewriting lobby hush into timeline. [player_name] felt the drawer watching her back as surely as Nolan did, and understood that opening it had already changed which soft she could still claim.
